title: HTTP & Web Architecture
hook: Browser meminta data, server menentukan respons
concept: Request terdiri atas method, URL, headers, dan body opsional. Response memiliki status, headers, dan body. Cookie sering membawa session ID, tetapi cookie sendiri bukan bukti bahwa pemiliknya boleh mengakses semua resource.
scenario: Saat membuka /api/orders/12, browser tidak langsung membaca database: server menerima request, mengenali sesi, memeriksa izin, lalu mengirim response.
request:
GET /api/orders/12 HTTP/1.1
Host: demo.local
Cookie: session=demo-andi
analysis: 200 OK berarti request berhasil diproses; bukan berarti endpoint aman. Pemeriksaan izin tetap diperlukan.
outcomes: GET cocok membaca resource; server mengirim 200 dengan data contoh.
POST dipakai membuat/mengirim data; endpoint contoh mengembalikan 201 Created.
DELETE memerlukan izin khusus; pada skenario contoh ditolak 403.

questions.q: Bagian HTTP yang menunjukkan aksi yang diminta?
questions.why: Method seperti GET atau POST menyatakan aksi pada resource.
403 Forbidden menandakan server memahami request tetapi menolak akses.
Status berhasil tidak membuktikan kontrol akses benar.
Response diawali status seperti HTTP/1.1 200 OK.
Cookie dapat mengaitkan request dengan sesi, bukan memberi hak otomatis.

en.hook: The browser requests data; the server decides how to respond.
en.concept: An HTTP request has a method, URL, headers, and sometimes a body. A response contains a status, headers, and a body. A session cookie identifies a session but does not automatically grant access to every resource.
en.scenario: When opening /api/orders/12, the browser does not read the database directly. The server receives the request, identifies the session, checks permissions, and returns a response.
en.analysis: 200 OK means a request was processed successfully; it does not prove the endpoint is secure. Access checks are still required.
outcomes: GET reads a resource; this example returns 200 OK and the requested data.
POST submits data to create a new resource; this example returns 201 Created.
DELETE attempts to remove a resource; the example user lacks permission, so the server returns 403 Forbidden.

questions.q: Which HTTP element describes the requested action?
questions.why: GET, POST, and DELETE are HTTP methods.
403 Forbidden means the server refuses the request.

questions.q: Does HTTP 200 prove an endpoint is secure?
questions.why: A successful response does not prove correct authorization.

questions.q: Where does the HTTP status code appear?
questions.why: The response starts with a status such as HTTP/1.1 200 OK.

questions.q: What does a session cookie usually carry?
questions.why: A cookie may identify a session but does not automatically grant permissions.

title: Web Reconnaissance
concept: Reconnaissance adalah pemetaan fitur, endpoint, parameter, dan teknologi yang terlihat. Tujuannya memahami cakupan pengujian yang diizinkan, bukan menebak celah tanpa arah.
scenario: Halaman produk memiliki endpoint /products, /api/search?q=, dan /api/products/:id. Setiap input membentuk permukaan uji yang berbeda.
analysis: Parameter q adalah input yang perlu diuji validasinya. Endpoint tersembunyi tidak otomatis rentan.
outcomes: Halaman memberi petunjuk fitur yang dapat diamati.
Endpoint adalah alamat fungsi aplikasi yang masuk cakupan.
Parameter adalah masukan yang perlu dicatat dan diuji terkontrol.

questions.why: Recon memetakan fitur, endpoint, parameter, dan teknologi.
q adalah parameter dalam URL.

questions.q: Apakah endpoint tak terlihat pasti rentan?
questions.why: Tidak terlihat di UI bukan bukti kerentanan.
Endpoint dan parameter membantu menentukan cakupan.
Recon harus berada dalam scope yang disepakati.

en.hook: Map the application before testing it.
en.concept: Reconnaissance maps visible features, endpoints, parameters, and technologies. Its purpose is to understand the authorized testing scope, not to guess vulnerabilities at random.
en.scenario: A product page uses /products, /api/search?q=, and /api/products/:id. Each input creates a different area to examine.
en.analysis: An undocumented endpoint is not automatically vulnerable. Record inputs and remain within the authorized scope.
outcomes: Pages reveal visible application features.
Endpoints identify functions within the authorized testing scope.
Parameters carry user input that should be documented and tested carefully.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of reconnaissance?
questions.why: Reconnaissance identifies features and inputs within the approved scope.

questions.q: Which example contains a query parameter?
questions.why: The q value after the question mark is a query parameter.

questions.q: Does an undocumented endpoint prove a vulnerability?
questions.why: An endpoint must be assessed before drawing conclusions.

questions.q: What must be established before testing?
questions.why: Authorization and scope define where testing is allowed.
Endpoints and parameters are important testing inputs.

title: Intercepting Proxy
hook: Amati lalu lintas, bukan hanya tampilan
concept: Intercepting proxy menempatkan alat inspeksi di antara browser dan aplikasi. Ia membantu melihat request sebenarnya, mengubah nilai uji, dan membandingkan response.
scenario: Tombol Bayar mungkin mengirim POST /api/checkout dengan body JSON. Mengubah angka di browser tidak berarti server akan mempercayainya.
analysis: Server harus menghitung ulang total dari data tepercaya, bukan menerima total dari klien begitu saja.
outcomes: Request asli diproses dengan total yang dihitung server.
Total dari klien berubah, tetapi tidak boleh dipercaya.
Server menghitung ulang dan menolak ketidaksesuaian.

questions.why: Proxy memeriksa lalu lintas request/response.
Proxy dapat melihat request yang melewatinya.
Server menghitung ulang berdasarkan data tepercaya.
Replay membantu pengujian terkontrol.

questions.q: Mengubah request berarti server pasti mengikuti?
questions.why: Server seharusnya memvalidasi seluruh input.

en.hook: Inspect requests before the server processes them.
en.concept: An intercepting proxy sits between the browser and server. It lets you inspect, modify, and replay requests in an authorized test environment.
en.scenario: A shopping cart sends a total price in a request. An attacker may change the value before it reaches the server.
en.analysis: Client-provided totals cannot be trusted. The server must calculate prices from trusted data.
outcomes: The original request uses the server-calculated total.
The client changes the total, but the server must not trust it.
The server recalculates the price and rejects mismatched values.

questions.q: What can an intercepting proxy inspect?
questions.why: A proxy can inspect requests and responses passing through it.

questions.q: Why is a client-supplied price risky?
questions.why: A client can modify its own request values.

questions.q: Where should a final price be calculated?
questions.why: The server should calculate trusted totals.
Replay resends a previously captured request.
Only systems within the permitted testing scope may be tested.

title: Authentication Testing
concept: Authentication memastikan identitas pengguna. Mekanisme login, reset password, MFA, sesi, dan logout membentuk satu siklus yang harus aman.
scenario: Sesi lama seharusnya tidak tetap berlaku setelah logout atau perubahan kredensial penting.
response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: sid=DEMO; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
analysis: Cookie sesi harus dilindungi; token contoh di slide bukan kredensial sungguhan.
outcomes: Login valid menghasilkan sesi contoh.
Kredensial salah ditolak tanpa mengungkap akun mana yang ada.
Sesi yang sudah logout harus ditolak.

questions.why: Authentication memastikan siapa pengguna.

questions.q: Apa yang harus terjadi setelah logout?
questions.why: Sesi harus tidak lagi diterima.
Pesan error tidak perlu mengungkap keberadaan akun.
HttpOnly membatasi pembacaan cookie oleh JavaScript.
MFA menambah faktor verifikasi.

en.hook: Logging in is only the start of session security.
en.concept: Authentication verifies identity. A secure session must be created, protected, expired, and revoked correctly.
en.scenario: A user signs in, receives a session identifier, then signs out. A copied old session must no longer work.
en.analysis: Logout should invalidate the server-side session, not merely hide the user interface.
outcomes: Valid credentials create a demonstration session.
Invalid credentials are rejected without revealing whether the account exists.
A session used after logout must be rejected.

questions.why: Authentication verifies who the user is.
Logout must invalidate the session server-side.

questions.q: What should happen to a wrong password?
questions.why: Invalid credentials must not authenticate the user.

questions.q: Why rotate session IDs after login?
questions.why: Rotating identifiers reduces session fixation exposure.

questions.q: Which cookie attribute helps prevent JavaScript access?
questions.why: HttpOnly prevents JavaScript from reading the cookie.

title: Authorization Testing
hook: Sudah login, boleh melihat data siapa?
concept: Authorization memeriksa apakah identitas tertentu boleh menjalankan aksi pada objek tertentu. Pemeriksaan harus dilakukan di server untuk setiap resource sensitif.
scenario: Andi memiliki pesanan 104, Budi memiliki 105. Mengganti ID di URL tidak boleh memberi Andi akses ke pesanan Budi.
analysis: IDOR terjadi bila server hanya mencari objek berdasarkan ID tanpa memeriksa kepemilikannya.
outcomes: Akses ke pesanan sendiri diizinkan.
Akses Andi ke pesanan Budi harus ditolak.
Tanpa sesi valid, server meminta autentikasi.

questions.why: Authorization mengecek izin aksi pada resource.
Jika diizinkan tanpa hak, itu broken object-level authorization.
Server menjadi otoritas keputusan akses.
ID sulit ditebak bukan pengganti authorization.
Akses fungsi role lebih tinggi tanpa izin adalah masalah vertikal.

en.hook: Being logged in does not grant access to every record.
en.concept: Authorization checks whether a particular user may perform an action on a particular object. Authentication and authorization solve different problems.
en.scenario: Andi requests his own order, then changes the order ID to one owned by Budi.
en.analysis: The server must check ownership and role for every request, not just the login state.
outcomes: Access to Andi’s own order is allowed.
Andi’s request for Budi’s order must be denied.
Without a valid session, the server requires authentication.

questions.why: Authorization enforces permissions for actions and objects.

options: Changing an object ID reveals another user’s data
questions.why: Missing object-level authorization may expose another user’s resource.

questions.q: What should happen when Andi requests Budi’s private order?
questions.why: The server must enforce ownership or other relevant access rules.
Authorization must be enforced at every protected operation.

questions.q: Is authentication the same as authorization?
questions.why: Identity verification and permission enforcement are different.

title: Injection Testing
concept: Injection muncul saat input tak tepercaya disisipkan ke interpreter sebagai bagian dari sintaks. Untuk SQL, gunakan parameterized query agar nilai tidak mengubah struktur perintah.
scenario: Pencarian produk aman memisahkan query SQL dari nilai pencarian. Penggabungan string membuka risiko perubahan logika query.
request:
// RENTAN
const sql = "SELECT * FROM items WHERE name= + q + ";
response:
// AMAN
db.query("SELECT * FROM items WHERE name = ?", [q]);
analysis: Perbedaan utamanya bukan karakter input, melainkan pemisahan antara kode SQL dan data.
outcomes: Input biasa mencari produk yang cocok.
Tanda kutip dapat merusak sintaks pada query yang digabung langsung.
Parameterized query memperlakukan seluruh input sebagai data.

questions.why: Pemisahan kode dan data gagal.
Parameter menjaga input sebagai nilai.
Validasi membantu, tetapi parameterisasi tetap diperlukan.
Parameterized query memperlakukan karakter input sebagai data.
Dampak bergantung pada hak database dan query.

en.hook: Keep user input separate from executable queries.
en.concept: Injection occurs when untrusted input is interpreted as part of a command or query. Parameterized SQL queries keep values separate from query syntax.
en.scenario: A search endpoint builds SQL by concatenating the search text directly into a query string.
en.analysis: A quote character may break an unsafe query; the solution is parameter binding, not simply blocking quotes.
outcomes: A normal search value returns matching products.
A quote may break an unsafe concatenated SQL query.
A parameterized query treats all supplied characters as data.

questions.why: Unsafe query construction can interpret user input as SQL syntax.
Bound parameters keep input data separate from SQL syntax.

questions.q: What may a quote character reveal?
questions.why: A quote can expose unsafe string-based query building.

questions.q: What does a parameterized query treat input as?
questions.why: Parameters are bound as values rather than executable syntax.

questions.q: Should error messages expose raw SQL?
questions.why: Detailed SQL errors should remain in internal diagnostics.

title: Client-Side Security
concept: XSS terjadi ketika data tak tepercaya diperlakukan sebagai markup atau script. CSRF berkaitan dengan request atas nama pengguna, sedangkan CORS mengatur akses respons lintas origin. Ketiganya berbeda.
scenario: Menampilkan komentar sebagai textContent berbeda dari memasukkannya langsung sebagai innerHTML.
analysis: Output encoding sesuai konteks mencegah browser menafsirkan data sebagai HTML aktif.
outcomes: Komentar biasa tampil sebagai teks.
Markup dari input tidak boleh dijalankan sebagai kode.
textContent menampilkan karakter HTML sebagai teks literal.

questions.why: textContent tidak menafsirkan input sebagai HTML.
XSS memanfaatkan interpretasi konten pada browser.
CSRF mengeksploitasi request lintas situs dengan otoritas korban.
CORS membatasi pembacaan respons lintas origin oleh browser.
Encoding dan API aman disesuaikan dengan konteks output.

en.hook: The browser has several different trust boundaries.
en.concept: Cross-site scripting, cross-site request forgery, and cross-origin resource sharing concern different browser security mechanisms. Context-aware encoding and server-side validation matter.
en.scenario: A website displays user comments, accepts state-changing requests, and communicates with other origins.
en.analysis: XSS, CSRF, and CORS are not the same vulnerability. Understand the trust boundary in each case.
outcomes: Plain comments are displayed as text.
HTML supplied by a user must not be executed as application code.
textContent displays HTML-like characters as literal text.

questions.q: What is a common XSS root cause?
options: Rendering untrusted input as executable markup
questions.why: Unsafe rendering can allow browser-side code execution.
textContent displays characters literally instead of parsing HTML.
CSRF abuses authenticated browser requests when defenses are missing.
CORS determines whether scripts from other origins may read responses.

questions.q: Are XSS and CSRF the same issue?
questions.why: They involve different trust boundaries and defenses.

title: File & Path Testing
hook: Nama file tidak boleh mengendalikan seluruh filesystem
concept: Path traversal terjadi ketika input path dapat keluar dari direktori yang diizinkan. Upload juga membutuhkan pemeriksaan tipe, lokasi penyimpanan, dan hak akses.
scenario: Aplikasi membaca documents/readme.txt. Jika menerima ../ tanpa batasan, proses dapat keluar dari folder documents.
analysis: Pemeriksaan prefix harus memakai path yang dinormalisasi dan batas direktori; symlink dan race condition perlu penanganan tambahan.
outcomes: File di direktori yang diizinkan dapat dibaca.
Percobaan keluar dari direktori dasar ditolak.
Subfolder yang berada dalam direktori dasar dapat diizinkan.

questions.why: .. merujuk ke direktori induk.
Normalisasi path tidak otomatis membatasi direktori.
Validasi upload harus berlapis.

questions.q: File di luar base directory seharusnya?
questions.why: Akses di luar direktori izin harus ditolak.
Symlink dapat melewati pemeriksaan path sederhana.

en.hook: File names must never bypass directory boundaries.
en.concept: File and path testing checks how an application validates file names, upload contents, storage paths, and access permissions.
en.scenario: A download endpoint reads a file name from a request and joins it with an uploads directory.
en.analysis: Normalize paths, enforce the permitted directory boundary, and check file permissions.
outcomes: An allowed file can be read from the permitted directory.
A path attempting to escape the base directory is rejected.
An allowed file in a subdirectory may be read if access rules permit it.

options: Escaping an allowed directory through path input
questions.why: Untrusted paths may reference files outside an allowed directory.

questions.q: Which input attempts to move to a parent directory?
questions.why: The ../ segment references a parent directory.

questions.q: What should a download endpoint verify?
questions.why: Validate the final resolved path and the user’s access rights.

questions.q: Can an allowed subfolder contain readable files?
questions.why: Access rules may permit files within approved subdirectories.

questions.q: Why is extension checking alone insufficient?
options: It does not establish content or permissions
questions.why: File type and access checks require more than the extension.

title: Security Misconfiguration
concept: Misconfiguration mencakup debug aktif di produksi, pesan error terlalu detail, header keamanan hilang, dan layanan administratif yang terekspos.
scenario: Kesalahan database tidak seharusnya menampilkan stack trace, query SQL, dan lokasi file internal kepada pengguna.
request:
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error

SQL syntax error at /srv/app/db.js:44
response:
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error

{"error":"Terjadi kesalahan. Coba lagi."}
analysis: Pesan publik dibuat generik; detail teknis tetap dicatat secara aman pada log internal.
outcomes: Debug publik dapat mengungkap detail internal.
Error generik tidak mengungkap implementasi.
Header keamanan menambah perlindungan sesuai konteks.

questions.why: Stack trace mengungkap file, fungsi, dan struktur.
Debug publik menambah paparan informasi.
Detail disimpan pada log internal.
Header membantu pertahanan sesuai konteks.
Paparan konfigurasi sering tampak di error atau layanan.

en.hook: Configuration mistakes can reveal internal details.
en.concept: Security misconfiguration includes verbose errors, exposed debugging, unnecessary services, and missing protections.
en.scenario: An application returns stack traces or database details directly to the browser when an error occurs.
en.analysis: Give users safe error messages and keep sensitive diagnostics in internal logs.
outcomes: Public debugging may expose internal implementation details.
A generic error avoids disclosing implementation details.
Security headers add context-dependent browser protections.

questions.why: Unsafe settings can expose information or increase attack surface.

questions.q: What should a public error show?
questions.why: Detailed diagnostics belong in protected logs.
Debug output may reveal paths, queries, and internals.

questions.q: Are security headers universally identical for every site?
questions.why: Header policies depend on the application’s architecture.

questions.q: Where should detailed errors be recorded?
questions.why: Internal logs can retain details without exposing them publicly.

title: Business Logic Testing
concept: Business logic flaw muncul ketika aturan proses dapat dilompati meskipun input dan sintaks tampak valid. Server harus memvalidasi urutan state dan aturan transaksi.
scenario: Diskon hanya boleh dipakai sekali, pembayaran harus selesai sebelum pesanan ditandai terkirim.
analysis: Server tidak boleh menerima perubahan state hanya karena klien meminta status tertentu.
outcomes: Urutan valid diterima.
Pengiriman sebelum pembayaran ditolak.
Kupon satu kali pakai ditolak saat percobaan kedua.

questions.why: Aturan workflow harus dipaksa server.
State transition harus divalidasi.
Aturan satu kali pakai tidak boleh hanya di UI.
State machine menggambarkan urutan valid.
Logika bisnis dapat salah meski sintaks valid.

en.hook: The correct sequence of business actions matters.
en.concept: Business logic security validates workflow transitions, transaction rules, prices, and single-use operations on the server.
en.scenario: A checkout workflow should require payment before shipping and must prevent a coupon from being redeemed twice.
en.analysis: Validate each state transition on the server and protect single-use actions against concurrent requests.
outcomes: A valid pay-then-ship sequence is accepted.
Shipping before payment is rejected.
A one-time coupon is rejected on its second use.

questions.q: What does business logic testing examine?
questions.why: Business logic tests whether application rules can be bypassed.
The example workflow requires successful payment first.

questions.q: What should happen to a single-use coupon after redemption?
questions.why: A single-use coupon must not be redeemed twice.

questions.q: Where should workflow transitions be validated?
questions.why: The server must enforce state transitions.
Concurrent requests may expose non-atomic single-use checks.

title: OWASP WSTG & Reporting
hook: Temuan yang baik harus dapat diverifikasi
concept: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide membantu menyusun pengujian sistematis. Laporan yang baik mencatat cakupan, langkah reproduksi, bukti, dampak, rekomendasi, dan retest.
scenario: Temuan IDOR perlu menunjukkan akun penguji, resource yang diminta, hasil yang tidak semestinya, serta pemeriksaan ulang setelah perbaikan.
request:
Finding: Akses objek tanpa pemeriksaan kepemilikan
Evidence: request, response, akun uji
response:
Remediation: enforce object-level authorization
Retest: akses silang ditolak
analysis: Hindari menyatakan severity tanpa menilai dampak dan konteks. Hilangkan data sensitif dari bukti.
outcomes: Pastikan target dan izin pengujian terdokumentasi.
Catat request/response yang relevan tanpa membocorkan rahasia.
Uji ulang perbaikan dan simpan hasilnya.

questions.why: WSTG menyusun metodologi pengujian.
Bukti perlu cukup untuk reproduksi tanpa membocorkan data.
Retest memverifikasi perbaikan.
Severity perlu mempertimbangkan konteks dan dampak.
Scope adalah batas legal dan teknis pengujian.

en.concept: The OWASP Web Security Testing Guide provides a structured approach to planning tests, gathering evidence, reporting findings, and verifying fixes.
en.scenario: A security tester records a reproducible issue, its impact, evidence, recommended fix, and retest results.
en.analysis: A report needs scope, reproducible steps, evidence, impact, remediation, and verification.
outcomes: Document the target and authorization scope.
Capture relevant request and response evidence without exposing secrets.
Retest the fix and record the outcome.

options: A structured web security testing guide
questions.why: WSTG provides guidance for structured web security testing.
Findings need reproducible evidence and a clear impact statement.
Scope documents what is permitted.
Retesting checks whether remediation resolved the issue.

questions.q: How should sensitive evidence be handled?
questions.why: Evidence should avoid unnecessary disclosure of sensitive data.
